findings: Cornell New York and North Carolina atlas pages direct users to their respective eBird portals.

The selected source records use CLO institutional identity and matching original/interpreted atlas collection codes. Each full occurrence URN includes its unchanged original collection code and OBS catalog identifier.

Connecting the literal internal atlas collection code to the corresponding public portal is an explicitly qualified interpretation; the primary pages do not define the GBIF collection-code mapping. Reputable EOD publisher identity and original record concordance supply the occurrence provenance.
Atlas membership is not proof of breeding, establishment, current persistence, individual human expert approval or survey negatives.
limitations: The third direct Cornell block request failed; its body is not cited as successfully acquired.
Earlier web-tool about-page retrieval timed out; cached web content is not represented as these raw HTTP bytes.
Only the explicitly reviewed collection allowlist is proposed. Unknown or contradictory collection and URN identities remain rejected.
